original_context_note: Compared spec.full_target literally with target-selection.json/full_target and problem.md:16-30: it retains the disclosed nonemptiness addition, the empty-set dimension convention, all nonnegative integer ambient dimensions, and the Euclidean coordinate product. Parameter n:N represents exactly that original domain, not an additional restriction. H001 is precisely nonemptiness (problem.md:16-22); H002 is precisely Euclidean compactness (21-23); both occur in the actual dependency closure and neither is unused. P is the complete equality on this domain. D001 supplies the Euclidean distance and zero-dimensional singleton; D002 is extended diameter with empty diameter zero; D003 retains verbatim the supplied infimum/supremum formulas and countable-cover/empty-member convention (only the dangling word 'This' after the definition was removed). D004-D006 record the native measure/dimension representation; R001 proves the normalization and critical-exponent bridge, so no measure identity is assumed by a definition. The native supremum convention gives empty-set dimension zero, consistent with the frozen convention. D007-D009 fix Lebesgue integration, I, and F; D010 initially has extended-real type, with finiteness proved only in N002. All ten definitions are total on their stated domains, have acyclic dependencies and require no hidden existence guard. The six selected M statements were compared with the actual successful pinned probe signatures: M001 is nonnegative integration of a countable a.e.-measurable series; M002 is the complete covering formula on Borel extended metric spaces; M003-M006 are the four exact dimension/measure implications for nonnegative exponents. I read their source contexts at Add.lean:320-372, Hausdorff.lean:235-260,510-574 and HausdorffDimension.lean:90-161. Their structural hypotheses and native [0,infinity] codomains are preserved. Ordered attempts to retrieve the exercise's book were unsuccessful; no result from that unavailable book is imported as E, and no deferred primary-source assumption is used. Every retained non-H proposition has one producer or a verified native source and lies in P's backward closure; the graph is acyclic. All original proof calculations and phases in problem.md:49-167 remain: box bound, interval partitions, positive-diameter replacement, product cost, open interval enlargements, fiber integration, both epsilon/scale limits, and the D>0/D=0 split. No material optional passage was omitted. This is an actual same-author inspection, not independent Audit A.

output_notes.note: R001/S001 proves H^s(A)=muH[s](A) for every Euclidean dimension m, arbitrary set A and positive s, including the finite/infinite scale and empty-member conventions. S002 exports all four critical-exponent implications and nonnegativity; no restriction to compact or measurable sets is inserted.

R002/S001 exports finiteness of every positive-exponent positive-scale content of E. S002 proves D<=n for n>=1 using the displayed C n^(a/2)h^(a-n) bound; S003 proves E=Eucl(0) and D=0 when n=0. Together with nonnegativity these give every clause of N002, notably the finiteness consumed by R004-R006.

R003/S001 proves all a>1 zero-measure claims by k^(1-a). S002 proves the coverwise diameter sum>=1 without cover-set measurability, and S003 proves the coverwise s-cost>=delta^(s-1) and the infinite measure limit for every 0<s<1. S004 applies N001 on the isometrically identified real line and derives dimension exactly one. The full estimates needed by R004 and R007 are exported, not merely the dimension equality.

R004/S001 closes the n=0 branch using only exported N002/N003 statements and an explicit distance-preserving transfer of arbitrary interval covers. S002-S004 prove the n>=1 branch with the original replacement budget, ceil partition estimate and constant 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1). F003 quantifies the cover scale/tolerance and F004 quantifies q>D. S005 takes q down to finite D and discharges the branch assumption, exporting the unconditional upper bound.

R005/S001-S005 proves H^s_delta(E)<=H^(s+1)_delta(F) for every positive s and delta on the identical Euclidean scale. The proof includes zero diameters, arbitrary nonmeasurable covers, finite c, an arbitrary countable cover, epsilon removal at fixed cover, and the infimum over all covers. Thus its exported statement suffices directly in R006 without any producer-only geometric detail.

R006/S001 applies N001 at exponent s with 0<s<D and N005 at the same scales, giving H^(s+1)(F)=infinity and dimension>=s+1. S002 uses 0<D<infinity to approach D from below and discharges L1, so the output is exactly the conditional positive-dimensional lower bound.

R007/S002 constructs j(t)=(x0,t) from H001, proves its distance identity and pulls back every cover of F to a no-more-expensive cover of I. N003 then gives H^s(F)=infinity for all 0<s<1. S003 uses N001, takes s up to 1, substitutes D=0 and discharges L1; the full conditional bound includes n=0.

R008/S001 uses N002 for the exhaustive nonnegative finite D cases, N006/N007 for the common lower bound, and N004 for the upper bound. Antisymmetry and expansion of D,F,I yield the full original equality in the specified Euclidean metric, including the zero-dimensional ambient case.
